item.title: Finally, a positive Penn State football report card in win vs Purdue
item.description: STATE COLLEGE — It was a strange to see in the late-afternoon sun on Halloween here − Nittany Lion running backs sprinting free and clear downfield. Yes, Penn State football , one of the worst rushing teams in the nation, enjoyed a resurgence of sorts on Saturday in Beaver Stadium against one of the most giving defenses around. First, senior tailback Carson Hansen cruised down the left side for 42 yards, by far his longest run of the season. A bit later, backup Cam Wallce broke in the clear to the right, going for 48 yards. Both runs set up first-half touchdowns as the Lions and coach Matt Campbell grinded down the Boilermakers and finally washed away their debilitating losing streak. It's almost difficult to lose when you nearly triple your opponent in total yards and time of possession. Rushing yards? Yes, this Penn State team dominated there, too, with a 269 to 33 advantage. Here are your grades from Penn State's 31-17 victory against Purdue in Beaver Stadium: Offense: B+ Penn State took advantage of what the Boilermaker defense gave them. Without its top two wideouts, the Lions worked their feeble run game and found success early and kept pounding it. They ran the ball 26 times in the first half, alone, and racked up 177 yards and scored twice. They were able to wear down the Boilermakers by holding the ball for a stunning 22 minutes before halftime. The Lions outgained Purdue by a stunning 423 yards to 151 with the game in doubt. Defense: A An impressive effort overall, particularly disrupting trending quarterback Ryan Browne. Slowing the run game was one thing but holding Browne to 8-of-20 passing and an interception through three quarters won them the game. They kept forcing a suspect and tiring Purdue defense back on the field, which all but sealed things. Special teams: C- It's difficult to make up for such an egregious failure on the second-quarter punt attempt that was blocked and returned for a touchdown. The Lions missed their blocking so badly on the play that punter Nathan Tiyce should have pulled in the ball and took the loss. We love Zay Robinson's punt returning potential, just not fair-catching balls inside the 10 yard line twice. A saving effort on the fake field goal early that turned three points into seven. Coaching: B+ We love the "aggressive" running game plan, especially missing your top two receivers and leaning on tailback Cam Wallace and his fresh legs. The Lions wore down the Boilermakers, running 58 plays, going for 200 yards-plus and holding the ball for an impressive 31:24 through just three quarters. Overall: A- It wasn't always pretty but this never really had to be, not when trying to stop a debilitating losing streak and save what's left of a season. So kudos to Campbell and staff for the game plan to wear out Purdue, for Becht for smart decision-making and this defense for suffocating everything good about the Boilermakers. item.title: Canelo Alvarez keeps career alive with vital win over Christian Mbilli
item.description: Canelo Alvarez scored a crucial win over Christian Mbilli on Saturday, rebounding from a loss to Terence Crawford after 13 months out of the ring. Alvarez outpointed Mbilli to take the WBC super-middleweight title from the Cameroonian, earning scorecards of 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110. Those scores factored in a docked point for Mbilli in round eight, after the champion landed one low blow too many for the referee’s liking, but it would have been a comfortable win for Canelo regardless. Canelo Alvarez (left) during his win over Christian Mbilli (Reuters) The Mexican icon was much more active than he had been in recent performances, starting well and – at times – matching the volume punching of Mbilli, who is known for his activity and had never lost before. Mbilli, 31, allowed that activity to dip here and there on Saturday, and Canelo, 36, capitalised well. The four-weight world champion varied his shots well, landing hard right hooks early on and mixing in uppercuts in the later rounds. Canelo appeared emotional afterwards, as he regained super-middleweight gold after losing his undisputed status against Crawford last year. Crawford claimed all the major belts by outpointing Canelo, before retiring from boxing in December. Upon the American’s retirement, Mbilli’s interim WBC belt was upgraded. But the Cameroonian’s first defence of the official title ended in disappointment, as Canelo got back to winning ways in Riyadh , which has been subjected to deadly attacks in recent weeks . The Yemen-aligned Houthis had launched numerous strikes on the Saudi city, injuring hundreds of people and killing more than 20, per local authorities. Canelo is a world champion once again (Reuters) Still, Saturday’s boxing event went ahead at ANB Arena, where Canelo said after winning: “It’s so difficult to explain [my emotions]. It’s something unbelievable. “This feels like my first title, now after 21 years as a professional; 16 years ago I won my first title, now I won the title again. I’m so proud, so proud of my team. [They] made me the champion I am.” “No, [nothing surprised me]. I knew he’s a strong fighter, and he didn’t throw a lot of punches because it’s difficult to throw punches with me. I did perfectly.”

item.title: Devils go top of EIHL with six-goal win over Flames
item.description: Cardiff Devils returned to the top of the EIHL table by beating Guildford Flames [Rebecca Brain] Cardiff Devils responded to their first home defeat of the season with a resounding 6-1 win over Guildford Flames at Vindico Arena. Having suffered a 4-1 loss to Belfast Giants on Wednesday evening, Devils recorded their biggest win of the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) so far. A fast start saw the Devils shoot to a four-goal lead inside the first quarter, with Nolan Yaremko, Brandon Estes, Panu Mieho and Ryan Barrow scoring. Yaremko added his second and Kohen Olischefski got in on the act in the second period before Justin Ducharme scored a consolation for the visitors. The win moves Devils back to the top of the table with 11 points from seven games, one ahead of both Giants, who have played a game fewer, and Sheffield Steelers. "I'm really happy. We let ourselves down with a horror show against Belfast on Wednesday, but I know the character of my team," said Devils head coach Paul Thompson. "We challenged them hard after that game, and like the good men and players I know they are, they responded. "We gave up 14 shots all night. Guildford looked more dangerous on the PK (penalty kill) than they did five-on-five. That is credit to our all-around game." Defeat ended Guildford's two-game league-winning run, though this is not their heaviest defeat of the season, having lost 10-2 against Fife Flyers. Devils are back in Challenge Cup at Manchester Storm on Sunday, 1 November, while Flames host Glasgow Clan, who are yet to win a point, in the EIHL.

item.title: Grades for Cincinnati Bearcats lopsided loss vs. No. 6 Utah Utes
item.description: The most frightening place to be for Halloween turned out to be a football field for Cincinnati Bearcats fans as they experienced a Nippert nightmare scary enough to drive off many of the 36,487 who attended. Just a week after knocking off No. 8 Texas Tech, UC was humbled by No. 6 Utah 49-25. The Bearcats outscored the Utes in the second half, but still lost by 24. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier was 22-for-29 for 260 yards and three touchdowns, two to tight end Hunter Andrews. UC's JC French IV was 16-for-30 for 263 yards and Cole Tabb had 131 yards rushing and a score for his fourth game over the century mark. Utah outgained UC 534 yards to 456, out-passed them 266-263 and outrushed them 268-193. UC was trying to make it back-to-back wins against Top 10 teams. Instead, they struggled to put 10 points on the board at halftime as the Utes had a 42-6 lead. It was enough to scare off an entire student section to more promising pumpkin patches. At the break, Utah's Dampier was 15-for-16 passing for a touchdown and the Utes had outrushed the Bearcats 197-72. UC drops to 5-3 (2-3 Big 12) and still needs a win to be bowl-eligible for a second straight season. Utah is now 8-0 (5-0 Big 12) going into their “Holy War” showdown with rival BYU Nov. 7. The Bearcats now look ahead to another ranked team as they’ll face the Houston Cougars on the road next weekend. The Cougars lost at Utah on Oct. 24, 21-13, and are 6-2 (3-2 Big 12). Here are grades from Cincinnati Bearcats vs. No. 6 Utah Utes Offense: C- Cole Tabb ran nine yards on UC's first play of the game, the Bearcats then couldn't gain a yard and had to punt, which set the tone for the day. Tabb would gain his yards, but the Bearcats got into the red zone twice and settled for field goals. One of those was missed. Gi'Bran Payne also fumbled, and Rabbit Evans returned it for a score that put Utah up 21-3 in the second quarter, a lead they doubled by halftime. Yards were somewhat deceiving as the Bearcats had chunk plays between the 20s. Tabb's 48-yard run was UC's first offensive touchdown, coming late in the third quarter. Defense: F+ The plus is for Jacob Finley's 79-yard pick-six, which gave the Bearcats their first touchdown. Everyone was aware of what Dampier and Wayshawn Parker could do, but no one figured the Utes would score nearly what they did in last year's game (45) by halftime. Utah's deceptive offense was a poison pill on the scary evening. Special Teams: C Max Fletcher had a 48-yard punt to begin the game. Stephen Rusnak was good from 47 yards early, then missed a 35-yarder before making one from 39 before halftime. It wasn't a game made for catching up by threes. item.title: Canelo Alvarez's Next Opponent Might Already Be Decided
item.description: Mexico's Canelo Alvarez reacts during the WBC super middleweight world championship bout against France's Christian Mbilli in Riyadh early on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Fayez NURELDINE / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images Canelo Alvarez looked great in Riyadh on Saturday night against Christian Mbilli. He outboxed him. He was slicker, had the more accurate punching, and had a much better understanding of how to win a round in big-time championship boxing. And as he mentioned, Mbilli’s style was just too simple . Because of that, Canelo is now the WBC super middleweight champion again, and he again looks like he could be the number one fighter at 168 pounds. With the WBC potentially having Lester Martinez aligned as the next man to challenge Canelo, that makes sense. Martinez was also present in Riyadh for the fight. But there was another fighter present who might also have somewhat of a promise to face Canelo in his next fight, and that was Hamzah Sheeraz. So which man gets the first crack at Canelo, now in his third reign as a super middleweight champion: Sheeraz or Martinez? Let’s talk boxing. Canelo Alvarez Next Fight Key Facts Detail Info Champion Canelo Alvarez, WBC super middleweight (third reign) Canelo’s record 63-3-2 Contender Hamzah Sheeraz, 24-0-1, former WBO super middleweight champion Contender Lester Martinez, 21-0-1, WBC interim super middleweight champion Canelo’s signature date Cinco de Mayo weekend The fight that makes the most sense is Sheeraz. Sheeraz is a long, lanky, powerful puncher who has, at times, looked great fighting at 168 pounds. But he’s also had situations where he hasn’t looked quite as good. His fight against Carlos Adames is one example. He also has a bit of a black mark against him in the eyes of some people throughout the boxing community. Sheeraz had an opportunity to fight Janibek Alimkhanuly, the former unified 160-pound champion who was moving up to 168 pounds. Rather than take that fight, Sheeraz vacated his WBO super middleweight title . There were questions surrounding that decision, including the possibility of an injury. During the broadcast of Canelo-Mbilli, Chris Mannix of DAZN has raised the possibility that Sheeraz’s decision could be connected to his chances of landing a fight with Canelo Alvarez, provided Canelo defeated Mbilli. That brings us to Martinez. Martinez makes sense because he was Mbilli’s last opponent before Saturday night’s loss to Canelo. They fought to a draw, and Martinez has since returned to the ring and picked up another victory . With Martinez also receiving an invitation to Riyadh, coming off a win, and having performed well against Mbilli, it makes sense that he could be the next fighter to challenge Canelo. There’s also the timing. If the fight takes place in May, around Cinco de Mayo, that’s an obvious date for Canelo. He practically owns that date in boxing whenever he’s available to fight. A matchup with Martinez would give Canelo another undefeated contender

item.title: What signing Lan Larison to the 53-man roster means for the Patriots
item.description: The New England Patriots have finally filled the open spot on their 53-man roster. Second-year running back Lan Larison, who started the season on the practice squad, was promoted to the active team ahead of its upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins. Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots. Improved running back depth The Patriots entered the weekend with three running backs on their active roster, but one of them as a question mark to actually suit up versus the Dolphins. It turns out, TreVeyon Henderson will indeed not participate in the game due to the illness that kept him out of practice on Thursday and Friday. Instead of using a practice squad elevation on Larison to bolster the depth, the Patriots have added him to their 53-man team. The full position depth chart now looks like this: 53-man roster (4): Rhamondre Stevenson (38), TreVeyon Henderson (32), Corey Kiner (9), Lan Larison (34) Injured reserve (1): RB Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending) What’s the benefit of brining Larison up instead of just elevating him? On the surface, there appears to be none. That said, besides the financial element we will get to in a second, the Patriots also add to their RB depth in a more sustainable manner: Larison was already standard-elevated for game day once, which in turn means he had only two such elevations left — a number that was effectively guaranteed to drop to one this weekend. Now on the 53-man team, those calculations no longer are a factor. Kickoff return considerations Entering Week 8, the Patriots are ranked 25th in the NFL in average kickoff return yards (24.9) and 27th in starting field position (28.5). There have been positive moments, but their kickoff return game has been relatively lackluster once again this year. Is Larison going to change this dramatically? He averaged 24.5 yards on his two runbacks earlier this year, which ranks above Kyle Williams’ 24.0 but below Corey Kiner’s 26.7. From that perspective, no massive spike should be expected. Still, his presence as an experienced runback option — he was a regular in that role throughout training camp — gives the Patriots some more flexibility. Not only could they decide to mix things up if performance calls for it, Larison also might help prevent exposing Kiner and Williams to extra contact. The team is getting quite thin at both running back and wide receiver and might need both of them on offense. Trade questions The NFL trade deadline is coming up on Nov. 10, and so far only one Patriots player — defensive tackle Christian Barmore — has been mentioned as a possible trade candidate . Should TreVeyon Henderson also be added to that list now that New England has signed another running back to the 53-man roster? There are potential arguments for him being available, including his rather uninspiring output so far in his sophomore campaign. item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 31: Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti walks along the sideline in the fist half of play during a college football game between the Minnesota Golden Gophers vs the Indiana Hoosiers on October 31, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana football got off to what’s now become a familiar start, with the defense dominating while the offense struggled to move the ball. Josh Hoover connected with Nick Marsh for a nine yard touchdown pass, on a two play, 14-yard drive set up by a Minnesota fumble that Indiana forced and recovered. The offense wasn’t the only thing Indiana struggled with in the first half. Billy Gowers had to punt more than you’d like, but he had some bad ones today, including a 15-yarder that set up Minnesota’s first field goal of the day. Nico Radicic was sent out for a 52-yard field goal, which was blocked. In the second quarter, he missed a 31-yarder. He redeemed himself with a 46-yarder that tied the game at 10 in the third quarter, but then didn’t even get a chance to tie it at 13 in the fourth quarter, after a bad snap that forced Indiana to just fall on the ball. Curt Cignetti opted for Grant Wilson in the second half, though it’s not yet clear whether that was due to Hoover’s accuracy, his injury status, or both. He took what looked like a tough shot to his shoulder again on an interception near the end of the first half and never reentered the game. Either way, by the time his day was over, Hoover finished 8/19 for 119 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Despite the special teams struggles earlier in the game Cignetti opted for a field goal with 3:48 left in the game, tying it at 13 after a ten play, 46-yard drive. item.title: Rapid Reaction: Oregon surges late, downs No. 20 Northwestern, 34-26
item.description: Nobody likes to lose. Nobody likes to lose a game they expect to win. And nobody likes to have a heap of momentum halted in an instant. No. 20 Northwestern (6-2, 3-2 B1G) experienced all of that this past weekend in Eugene. Against a reeling Oregon (5-3, 3-2 B1G), missed tackles, miscommunication in the secondary and late offensive line struggles led to the Wildcats’ demise. Aidan Chiles’ herculean effort – 374 total scrimmage yards and a 128.7 quarterback rating – went by the wayside in a 14–point fourth quarter by the Ducks’ offense. For the first time this season, NU pieced together points on its opening drive of an away tilt, as Chiles completed three of his first five passes. His 15-yard scramble helped him escape an early sack on a 3rd-and-8 from the Wildcats’ 33-yard line – the turning point of what would be an 11-play, 63-yard drive, ending with a 37-yard field goal from Jackson Kleather. A brief three-and-out from the Oregon offense followed, and when Northwestern had its chance, Chiles fired a 64-yard strike to Griffin Wilde to make the advantage two scores with 5:57 to go in the first quarter. CINEMA. pic.twitter.com/F0j88tdPrD — Northwestern Football (@NUFBFamily) October 31, 2026 Wilde’s first-quarter score marked the first time he’s logged back-to-back touchdowns in Big Ten play since last October. Mighty Oregon wasn’t okay with letting two early Northwestern scores snowball into making Saturday’s contest an uncompetitive one. The Ducks sewed together a three-point scoring drive in the back end of the first, starting with Dierre Hill Jr.’s 54-yard kickoff return. Jordan Davidson followed with a 12-yard rush, then Dylan Raiola fired a laser to Evan Stewart to get OU inside Northwestern’s 10, but that’s as far as it got downfield. NU’s opponents had a 39.1% touchdown conversion rate from inside the red zone entering Saturday’s contest – the embodiment of the Wildcats’ “bend, don’t break” philosophy. They held to it when tested for the first time in Eugene, holding the Ducks to a field goal to preserve a 10-3 lead heading into the second quarter. The ‘Cats countered with a field goal of their own after a methodical 56-yard drive bled 6:11 off the clock. item.description: Karlsruhe’s Maximilian Senft reflects on Frank Schmidt coaching documentary that inspired his career Karlsruher SC head coach Maximilian Senft celebrated an especially meaningful victory on Saturday evening. Following his team’s hard-fought 2-1 win over 1. FC Heidenheim, the Austrian trainer revealed that opposing coach Frank Schmidt had been one of the figures who inspired him to pursue a career in football management. Speaking at the post-match press conference at the Wildparkstadion, Senft explained that he had been influenced by Schmidt’s appearance in the acclaimed 2013 German football documentary Trainer! , directed by filmmaker Aljoscha Pause. The revelation added an unusual personal dimension to an important evening for Karlsruhe. Senft’s team had climbed out of the relegation zone with a deserved victory over Heidenheim , securing only their third league win of the campaign. Senft recalls how Frank Schmidt inspired him Senft addressed his counterpart directly toward the end of his opening statement, after reflecting on Karlsruhe’s performance and the significance of the three points. “Frank, I’d like to wish you a safe journey home,” Senft began before sharing a personal recollection. “Just on a personal note, I mentioned this before the match as well. I started my coaching career approximately ten years ago. I don’t know how many of you are familiar with the film Trainer! , but Frank was one of the main protagonists.” “He was one of the first coaching personalities who inspired me along my journey,” Senft continued. “So, irrespective of the result, this was a very special match for me today. Schmidt, who had remained largely stone-faced and emotionless throughout the proceedings, briefly broke from his otherwise impassive demeanour. It was a small gesture, but one that underscored the personal significance of Senft’s remarks. item.description: Sovereignty, ridden by Junior Alvarado, crosses the finish line to win the Breeders' Cup Classic (Tanner Pearson) Sovereignty won the $7 million Breeders' Cup Classic at Keeneland on Saturday, denying Forever Young a rare repeat in the showpiece of the racing extravaganza. Trained by Bill Mott and ridden by Junior Alvarado, 2025 Kentucky Derby winner Sovereignty seized his first chance at the Classic after he was scratched from last year's edition because of a fever. He was beaten twice to open his 2026 campaign, and his Classic participation was again threatened by a hoof abscess, but Alvarado said he never doubted that Sovereignty could win the Classic. "What he did today, Sovereignty, it's just spectacular," Alvarado said. "We really wanted to run so bad the Classic last year. I'm just so glad the Godolphin team gave us a chance to keep him in training and get to do what he did today." Sovereignty settled in well behind pace-setting stablemate Knightsbridge and left no doubt when Alvarado set him loose at the top of the stretch. He finished ahead of The Puma, with Knightsbridge third. "Turning in the back side ... I was like oh boy, it's like I can't wait to turn for home because I knew the power I have underneath me," Alvarado said. "The way he was traveling the whole time, letting me know, like, I'm here for you. I never had a doubt the whole way around." Forever Young, who gave Japan a first Classic winner at Del Mar last year, ran just behind Knightsbridge for much of the way but faded to finish fifth. The well-traveled star trained by Yoshito Yahagi had been vying to join Tiznow as the only horses to win back-to-back Breeders' Cup Classics. Yahagi said he thought jockey Ryusei Sakai had Forever Young perfectly positioned but when it came to the stretch run "there was no response". "I feel apologetic, but above all I'm relieved that the horse came back safely," Yahagi said. item.title: Three Takeaways From Penn State’s Win Against Purdue
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; University Park, Pennsylvania, USA; Penn State Nittany Lions head coach Matt Campbell (right) talks with Purdue Boilermakers head coach Barry Odom (left) during a warmup prior to the their game at West Shore Home Field at Beaver Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Breathe. Penn State has a conference win. The Lions knocked off Purdue on Saturday and here were some of the big takeaways from Penn State improving to 4-4. Aggressive Matt Campbell One of our biggest complaints on this blog – and on the BSD Podcast, you should tune in right now and subscribe on YouTube – is that Matt Campell has been far too conservative. Maybe it was the pressure of a four-game losing streak, but Campbell looked more aggressive in this game. In the first half, there was the fake field goal to set up Penn State’s first score, then a fourth down attempt in the second quarter deep in his territory, and even his aggression when he was upset with the game’s officiating. It was a different approach in attitude than he had against USC (where he settled for field goals) or Northwestern (where he basically gave up and punted in the second half). Now, will it continue for Penn State’s last four games? We’re a Cam Wallace Blog Now Cam Wallace, who was buried on the depth chart, got the game’s first carry. The Big Ten Network broadcast made mention of how the coaching staff had been impressed with his work during the bye week and that he was going to get some more touches. But we had no idea how much! Wallace turned in the best game of his injury riddled Penn State career, going for more than 100 yards and a score. Quinton Martin was nowhere to be seen on Saturday and James Peoples got just a few snaps. Instead, it was Wallace and Carson Hansen who got the bulk of the carries in Penn State’s best rushing game of the conference season. Can ANYONE Sack the Quarterback? Ok, let’s talk one negative thing about this win. Penn State certainly hassled and harassed Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne all day. But the Lions still couldn’t come up with a sack…until the last two minutes of the game. The Boilers’ first touchdown came on a play where Browne simply threw the ball up for grabs under duress – but not enough duress where he was sacked. Is there any way that Penn State can find a bit of a pass rush threat in the last month of the season?

The seven-time F1 champion beat Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds as the two drivers who can potentially stop Kimi Antonelli clinching the world title on Sunday locked out the front row. Antonelli qualified fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, but will start fourth because of a one-place penalty for the Dutchman. The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and the Italian finishes lower than ninth, or if Hamilton wins and Antonelli is out of the points. Hamilton's pole is his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, three years and three months ago, and the 105th of his career. He is the oldest driver to secure a pole since Mario Andretti for Ferrari at the 1982 Italian Grand Prix. He and Russell both went out early for their first runs and had to watch as their rivals sought and failed to beat them. Leclerc went first, falling short of Hamilton by 0.119secs. Antonelli was never on target but Verstappen was fastest of all after two sectors and on course to take pole. But the Dutchman locked up into the hairpin in the stadium section and ruined his lap. "Oh man, I'm lost for words," said Hamilton. "It's been a really challenging weekend - we had the engine issue yesterday, which meant we were on the back foot and didn't do a long run. "We've done a really good job on the setup and to have pole here, wow, it feels special. It's my first pole for Ferrari, and 105th, I like that number. "To have your first Ferrari pole, it takes me back to watching Michael [Schumacher] get all those poles when he was at Ferrari and all those wins." Hamilton had been only fourth on the first runs, more than 0.4secs off Leclerc's pace-setting time. But on his final run, he said: "I don't think I lost any time anywhere. It was a super-good lap." After storming to the Championship title last season to secure their return to the top flight for the first time since 2001, Frank Lampard's side were given little time to settle into their new surroundings when the campaign began in August. By the end of their first month back in the Premier League, Coventry were rooted to the bottom of the table, having lost all four of their matches by a combined score of 10-0. The final defeat of that brutal introduction - a 5-0 hammering at the hands of high-flying Brighton - was enough to convince even the most optimistic supporters that a return to the Championship could be on the cards. But since that humbling defeat on the south coast almost six weeks ago, Lampard's side have breathed new life into their campaign, winning three of their next five matches. After back-to-back victories over Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United in September, Saturday's 3-1 win over Sunderland lifted the Sky Blues to 15th in the table. Coventry are not the only newly promoted side to have impressed, with former Championship rivals Ipswich Town and Hull City also making encouraging starts. The three teams have collected a combined 31 points after nine games, the 13th-highest tally by promoted sides at this stage in Premier League history. Hull and Ipswich account for 22 of those points, with Sergej Jakirovic and Gary O'Neil's sides both sitting on 11. Coventry are slightly behind their promoted peers, but the Sky Blues' three victories have still earned them a respectable nine points. And there is further encouragement for the newcomers - since the 2010-11 season, all 18 promoted teams who have collected at least 11 points from their opening nine games have avoided relegation. item.description: Hoggard girls tennis had no tricks up its sleeve this Halloween, just one historic treat for Wilmington: the program's first state championship. The Vikings capped their dominant 2026 season with a 5-1 victory over Myers Park on Friday, Oct. 31, at the Burlington Tennis Center to claim the NCHSAA 8A dual-team state championship. With the win, Hoggard (19-1) became the first New Hanover County tennis team, boys or girls, to win an NCHSAA dual-team state title. And the dominance started right away. Fresh off winning an individual singles state championship, Hoggard sophomore Braelyn Roberson had little trouble at No. 1 singles, cruising to a 6-2, 6-1 victory. item.title: Georgia 27, Florida 8: Bulldogs bruise Gators, cruise to another Cocktail Party win
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 31: Nate Frazier #3 of the Georgia Bulldogs reacts after rushing for a touchdown against DJ Coleman #33 and Myles Graham #5 of the Florida Gators during the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Only two weeks ago I noted in this space that if your college football team goes -3 or so in the turnover column you’re going to lose just about every college football game you play. I am absolutely delighted to report that is still true. Florida needed to play a clean football game to stay in the game against Georgia and did the opposite of that, turning the ball over four times as the Bulldogs never really sweated. The Georgia offense was not its most impressive. To be fair, the Bulldogs never felt like they needed to get the offense out of second gear, controlling the clock and field position almost from the outset. Still Georgia fans would have liked to see the Bulldogs never offense show a little more explosiveness. The most explosive aspects of the Red and Black attack this afternoon were the explosive number of screen passes and the explosive number of Gunner Stockton keepers. I didn’t start counting the screen passes seriously until we got to 8, and I still don’t fully understand what was going on there. It was as if Mike Bobo saw the Gators’ beleaguered secondary and decided to give those guys a break. Gunner Stockton carried the ball 12 times for 46 tough yards on the day, and was equally pedestrian in the passing game, going 13 for 23 for 101 yards and no touchdowns. When Stockton threw a shoulder into Gator Myles Graham to stop his return of a Talyn Taylor fumble he sealed a career first: the first game in which he has had more tackles (1) than touchdown passes (0). I have every reason to believe the Bulldogs could have scored more points and showed more wrinkles had Coach Smart and Coach Bobo felt it necessary. It wasn’t, and they disn’t. But next week’s showdown with a high octane Ole Miss attack is likely to be different. But on the bright side, the Bulldog defense uncorked one on the Gators for the ages. Only on their last drive did the Gators finally pass Gunner Stockton alone in rushing yards. The Athenians came close to ending Florida’s nation-leading streak of avoiding shutouts, which now stands at 481 games. item.title: Canelo Alvarez wins decision over undefeated Christian Mbilli to become champion again
item.description: ﻿Christian Mbilli and Canelo Alvarez | Fayez Nureldine, AFP via Getty Images Canelo Alvarez didn’t waste any time getting gold around his waist again. The multi-time, multi-division champion won a workmanlike decision over Christian Mbilli (29-1-1) in Saturday’s main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to reclaim the WBC super middleweight title he lost to Terence Crawford in September 2025. It was far from Canelo’s most thrilling performance, but Mbilli rarely threatened to finish and showed little comeback gusto in the championship rounds. In the end, the judges scored the 12-round fight 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110 in favor of Canelo (64-3-2). Afterwards, Canelo spoke about the emotions that came with once again being a champion. “It’s so difficult to explain,” Canelo said. “It’s something unbelievable. It feels like my first title. Now, after 21 years as a professional, 16 years ago I won my first title. Now I won that title again. I’m so proud of my team.” He also joked that his wife told him not to come home if he didn’t leave Saudi Arabia with the WBC title. It was clear early on there would be no problems in the Alvarez household, despite Mbilli showing off the volume punching that earned him the interim WBC title—later elevated to undisputed status following Crawford’s retirement—and saw him go undefeated in his first 30 pro bouts. Unfortunately for Mbilli, Canelo’s counters and body work seemed to slow the champion down and he never found an extra gear to put away his more famous challenger. In Round 7, Canelo caught Mbilli with an uppercut that stood as the hardest punch of the fight to that point, and then the bout took another turn in the eighth, where Canelo had the advantage that became even more pronounced on the scorecards when Mbilli was docked a point for an illegal blow to the back of the head. From there, Canelo stayed in a steady rhythm, doing just enough to keep Mbilli from initiating any significant offense and cruising to a decision win. In his post-fight interview, Canelo was non-commital as far as what could be next for his 70th fight, only saying he planned to take a two-week vacation and get back in the gym.
